candidates.tagline: 8 years of 'almost ready' — Tesla's flying Roadster demo is happening, driver not invited
candidates.story: Tesla's next-gen Roadster with SpaceX cold-gas thrusters has missed at least eight deadlines since 2017; the August 2026 demo will be remotely operated with no driver inside because the thruster noise and force make it unsafe to occupy, and spectators must stand hundreds of yards away — a brief hover a few inches off the ground is the scaled-back reality of a car that was once supposed to drive upside-down on a magnetised roller-coaster ramp.
candidates.why_funny: A car company delayed a 'flying' vehicle for nearly a decade only to produce a demo where nobody is allowed near it and the vehicle barely leaves the tarmac.
candidates.alt: The second-generation Tesla Roadster concept car — a low-slung red sports car with a frameless windshield and aggressive wedge profile — shown at its 2019 preview event

candidates.tagline: Billions spent on space-age electromagnetic catapults — now the Navy is going back to steam
candidates.story: On August 13, 2026, Trump signed a directive ordering Ford-class aircraft carriers to replace EMALS — the electromagnetic launch system the Navy spent $4+ billion extra on because steam was 'outdated' — with steam catapults starting from the USS Doris Miller (CVN-81); the catch is that nobody in the US has built a steam catapult in roughly twenty years, the reversal will cost billions more and could delay the carrier from 2034 to the end of the next decade.
candidates.why_funny: The US Navy replaced steam catapults with billion-dollar electromagnetic ones because steam was old-fashioned, then ordered the billion-dollar electromagnetic ones replaced with steam because steam is reliable — making both decisions simultaneously correct and catastrophically expensive.
candidates.alt: The USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78), the lead Ford-class aircraft carrier, photographed at sea near the Solent off the English coast in 2022 — the class whose EMALS electromagnetic launch system is at the centre of the reversal decision
